title: Some historians say he beat Marconi to radio waves. He never patented it.

sources.text: MapsOfIndia - 23rd November 1937: Jagadish Chandra Bose passed away

caption:
Some historians say he beat Marconi to radio waves. He never patented it.

Bose demonstrated wireless signal transmission using microwaves as early as 1895 and was among the first to use a semiconductor junction to detect radio waves - work that predates Guglielmo Marconi's famous demonstrations, though Bose never patented it.

His crescograph could detect and record subtle plant movements invisible to the naked eye. In 1917, he founded the Bose Institute in Kolkata, often called the first interdisciplinary research centre in Asia.

Bose's refusal to patent his radio work meant less personal gain, but it set a precedent for Indian science as something built in the open, for everyone to build on.
